case_title: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Killu @ Kailash and Ors.
aggravating_circumstances: Members of an unlawful assembly, use of deadly weapons, nighttime assault
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 r/w. s.149 IPC
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302 r/w. s.149 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution alleged that five individuals entered the house of the deceased during the night and inflicted injuries on him, resulting in his death. The deceased was found with two fatal injuries, and the medical evidence confirmed that these injuries were inflicted before his death. The accused were armed with various weapons, including an axe, Ballam, and lathi. The trial court convicted all five accused under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC, citing their involvement in an unlawful assembly with a common object of causing death. The High Court acquitted three of the accused, arguing that they did not use deadly weapons and did not directly cause the injuries. However, the Supreme Court overturned this decision, emphasizing that the presence of all five accused in the house, their armed status, and the common object of the assembly established vicarious liability under Section 149 IPC.
